question: Which Indian dance form is Darshana Jhaveri the leading exponent of ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Darshana Jhaveri** is one of the leading exponents of the **Manipuri dance form**, which is one of the major Indian classical dance styles.
 
• Manipuri dance, also known as **Jagoi**, is particularly known for its **graceful and fluid movements**.
 
• This dance form primarily originates from the state of **Manipur** in northeastern India and is deeply connected to the region's folk traditions and rituals.
 
• Darshana Jhaveri and her sisters have significantly contributed to the popularization and preservation of Manipuri dance across India and the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi**

 
 
• Originating from the state of **Odisha**, Odissi is one of the oldest surviving dance forms of India.
 
• It is known for its **tribhangi (three bends) posture** and intricate footwork.
 
• Odissi dance is characterized by its fluid movements, expressive gestures, and strong narrative element, often depicting stories from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Hailing from the state of **Andhra Pradesh**, Kuchipudi is renowned for its fast rhythms and dramatic characterization.
 
• It often involves a combination of **dance, music, and acting**.
 
• This dance form is traditionally performed as dance-dramas, with themes typically revolving around stories from the Hindu epics.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form that originated in the northern regions of India.
 
• It is characterized by its intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures, often telling stories through dance.
 
• Kathak has a strong connection to the Bhakti movement and the Mughal era, reflecting a blend of Hindu and Persian influences.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri**
 
 
• Manipuri dance is deeply rooted in the rituals and culture of the people of **Manipur**.
 
• It is known for its **graceful, fluid, and delicate movements**, which are often inspired by themes of love and devotion.
 
• The dance is performed as a part of religious ceremonies and festivals, particularly the **Ras Leela**, which depicts the love story of Radha and Krishna.
